meta.disclaimer: This is an unofficial, community-maintained reference. Specifications are compiled from GameSir's official product pages, manuals and FAQ documents, from independent measurement data published by gamepadla.com, and from published reviews. Figures are not the result of first-hand testing by the maintainers unless explicitly labelled as such. Where a value could not be verified against a source it is left blank rather than estimated. Corrections with a source are welcome.

controllers.name: GameSir Cyclone 2
controllers.tagline: An Xbox-layout tri-mode wireless controller with Mag-Res TMR sticks, micro-switch face buttons and dual-mode Hall Effect triggers, measured among the lowest-latency controllers in its price class.
controllers.msrp: $49.99 / £49.99 standalone, $55.99 / £55.99 for the charging-dock bundle (launch pricing, 26 November 2024)

connectivity.notes: Tri-mode: USB-C wired, 2.4GHz dongle, Bluetooth. Explicitly NOT compatible with Xbox consoles. Input modes are XInput, DS4, NS and HID, cycled by holding View + Menu. Switch 2 support is claimed on retail listings. The included aluminum charging dock has a USB port, and GameSir recommends plugging the dongle into the dock to keep it close to the controller.

sticks.measuredNotes: Measured by gamepadla Stick Tracer on firmware 3.5.2, single unit, recording no inner deadzone and 0.0% circle error. A separate reviewer using gamepadla tooling measured 0.8-1.0%, so results vary between units and firmware. Right-stick asymmetry measured notably higher than the left, 10.2% against 3.4%.

triggers.tech: Precision-tuned Hall Effect analog triggers with a physical micro-switch hair-trigger lockout
triggers.notes: Physical trigger locks toggle between Hall Effect analog travel and mechanical micro-switch actuation. A separate software hair-trigger mode is available via key combo for FPS and action games. On-board calibration is supported for triggers, sticks and gyro.

controllers.dpad: Tactile-switch D-pad, fully fenced. Reviewers describe it as clicky and precise.
controllers.faceButtons: Micro-switch (esports-grade) ABXY rated to 5 million clicks, with light actuation and short throw. A Nintendo layout mode is available by holding a combo for 2 seconds; the default is the Xbox layout. Reviewers note the clicky micro-switches are divisive — noticeably louder and firmer than membrane alternatives.

pollingRate.pc: 1000 Hz (wired and 2.4GHz dongle); Gamepadla measured 1000-1002 Hz median
pollingRate.notes: Xbox consoles are not supported. Bluetooth is rated 250 Hz and Gamepadla measured roughly 250-400 Hz there. This is the strongest-measuring controller covered on this site: Gamepadla recorded 2.33 ms average button latency and 4.70 ms stick latency wired with only 0.28 ms jitter, and 7.4 ms button latency via dongle, earning a LatScore of A wired / B wireless. Bluetooth averaged around 6 ms but with spikes over 26 ms and 3.85 ms jitter.

battery.claimedLife: Manufacturer estimate of about 10 hours. GameSir does not publish a figure on its product page; TechRadar states GameSir gave the 10-hour estimate on request, and a GameSir-affiliated store lists '8-10 hours with lighting.'
battery.notes: Independent measurements land at the low end of that estimate: roughly 8 hours with RGB and rumble active (Pocket-lint), and Neowin recorded approximately 8 hours minimum with lighting enabled. GameSir Connect shows only a color-coded battery indicator, not a percentage. Charges via USB-C or the included aluminum charging tower, which starts charging automatically when the controller is set down.

extraButtons.notes: Two fully remappable back buttons plus an M button. Four hot-swappable profiles are stored on the controller itself, so settings persist without the software running; the active profile is shown by four illuminated segments in the center of the controller. Macro and turbo are supported.

gyro.notes: 6-axis gyroscope, active in Switch mode and manually activatable elsewhere. On-board gyro calibration is supported.

controllers.rumble: Two asymmetric rumble motors, one in each grip. Vibration intensity is adjustable via a button combo as well as in software. Reviewers also note wireless audio support alongside the 3.5mm jack.

faceplates.notes: No swappable faceplate system. GameSir does sell detachable joystick caps for the Cyclone 2 as a separate accessory, and the stock caps are thick Sony-style with anti-friction metal necks. The shell uses translucent plastic with an RGB strip in each grip and around the center button.

notableFeatures: Lowest measured wired latency of any controller covered here: 2.33 ms average button latency with 0.28 ms jitter, rated LatScore A wired by gamepadla
Mag-Res TMR sticks with 12-bit / 4096-point sampling and no inner deadzone measured
Micro-switch ABXY rated to 5 million clicks, plus a fully fenced tactile-switch D-pad
Physical trigger locks convert Hall Effect analog triggers to mechanical micro-switches
Four hot-swappable profiles stored on the controller, so it works fully configured without software running
3.5 mm headphone jack, which the Super Nova and multiplatform Tarantula Pro both lack
Aluminum auto start-stop charging tower with dongle storage in the bundle edition
Swappable stick caps with anti-friction metal necks
Turbo with four modes: Slow 8Hz, Medium 12Hz, Fast 20Hz, Off

knownIssues.symptom: The 2.4GHz dongle connection keeps dropping, sometimes with jittery button and stick input.
knownIssues.cause: Mismatched controller and dongle firmware is the primary cause. GameSir also cites RF interference from 8K wireless devices and NearLink devices, and thick obstructions between the dongle and controller.
knownIssues.fix: Match the firmware: dongle V1.1.9 or above AND controller V3.4.4 or above — GameSir stresses that updating one requires updating the other. Update the dongle from GameSir Connect while the controller is connected through it, or force it by holding the dongle's sync button as you plug it in (the light should stay off) with Connect open. Update the controller by plugging it in via cable and pressing 'update firmware', or force it by holding Logo + Menu while plugging it in with Connect open. For interference, move the dongle closer using a USB extension or the charging dock's USB port.

knownIssues.symptom: The controller shows a blue rather than green indicator light when connected to a PC, and games behave incorrectly.
knownIssues.cause: The controller has been accidentally switched into DS4 or NS input mode instead of XInput.
knownIssues.fix: Hold the View button + Menu button to cycle between XInput, NS and DS4 modes. XInput, indicated by a green light, is the correct mode for most PC use and is required for GameSir Connect.

knownIssues.symptom: The controller will not power on at all after a firmware upgrade failed in GameSir Connect.
knownIssues.cause: Interrupted or failed firmware flash leaving the controller soft-locked. TheSixthAxis describes this as a known bug affecting both the Cyclone 2 and Super Nova.
knownIssues.fix: Reset the controller by poking the reset hole on the back with a small object, then retry the update.

knownIssues.symptom: A single button press registers as continuous rapid presses and the light flashes red.
knownIssues.cause: Turbo (rapid-fire) mode is enabled.
knownIssues.fix: Double-tap the M button to turn turbo off.

knownIssues.symptom: Cannot connect over Bluetooth or dongle; the indicator light keeps blinking slowly.
knownIssues.cause: Slow blinking means reconnecting mode — the controller is trying to reach a previously paired device rather than accepting a new one.
knownIssues.fix: Hold the Home Button + Share Button for 2 seconds to force pairing mode; the light should then blink fast. For a dongle connection, also hold the pairing button on the dongle so the two re-pair.

knownIssues.symptom: GameSir Nexus does not recognize the Cyclone 2.
knownIssues.cause: Wrong application — the Cyclone 2 is a GameSir Connect device. Nexus is only for GameSir's Xbox-licensed controllers.
knownIssues.fix: Use GameSir Connect with the controller connected via dongle or cable in XInput mode.

knownIssues.symptom: Stick drift or trigger problems during use.
knownIssues.cause: Sticks or triggers out of calibration.
knownIssues.fix: Run the on-board Stick & Trigger Calibration procedure from the manual; GameSir links a Cyclone 2 specific calibration tutorial video from the FAQ page. Deadzones can also be tuned in GameSir Connect or on-board.

faq.q: Which software does the Cyclone 2 use?
faq.a: GameSir Connect, connected via dongle or cable in XInput mode. GameSir Nexus does not support it. The Cyclone 2 is explicitly listed among GameSir Connect's compatible products on GameSir's downloads page.

faq.q: What platforms does the Cyclone 2 support?
faq.a: Switch, iOS, Android, PC and Steam. It is NOT compatible with Xbox consoles.

faq.q: What firmware versions do I need for reliable dongle operation?
faq.a: Dongle V1.1.9 or above and controller V3.4.4 or above. GameSir stresses these must be updated together — updating the dongle without updating the controller to the latest version causes disconnections.

faq.q: How do I switch between XInput, Nintendo Switch and DS4 input modes?
faq.a: Hold the View button + Menu button. XInput, shown by a green indicator light, is the standard mode for PC.

faq.q: How do I force the controller back into pairing mode?
faq.a: Hold the Home Button + Share Button for 2 seconds; the indicator should switch from slow blinking to fast blinking. For dongle pairing, also press the pairing button on the dongle.

faq.q: How are the triggers configured?
faq.a: The Hall Effect analog triggers give linear input suited to racing games. A key combo switches them to hair-trigger mode for FPS and action games, and physical trigger locks toggle between Hall Effect analog and micro-switch actuation.

faq.q: How many mappable buttons does the Cyclone 2 have?
faq.a: Two mappable back buttons. The controller also stores four hot-swappable profiles on-board, indicated by the four lit segments in the center.

faq.q: How long does the battery last?
faq.a: GameSir estimates about 10 hours from the 860mAh cell, provided to TechRadar on request. Independent testing lands nearer 8 hours with RGB and rumble active. GameSir Connect shows only a color-coded indicator rather than a percentage.

faq.q: Does it have a headphone jack?
faq.a: Yes, a 3.5mm headphone jack on the bottom edge. TechRadar notes this as a bonus over the Super Nova, which lacks one.

controllers.name: GameSir G7 HE
controllers.tagline: Officially Xbox-licensed wired controller that keeps the G7 SE's Hall Effect sticks and triggers but swaps in microswitch face buttons and d-pad, adds silicone grips, and drops the back-button lock latches.

connectivity.notes: Wired only, via a 3 m detachable USB-C cable. No battery and no wireless mode. GameSir's product page additionally lists Steam as a supported platform; the manual tech-spec block also lists Android, but this is not repeated on the product page or FAQ and is unconfirmed.

sticks.durability: Up to 5 million cycles (GameSir manufacturer claim, from the G7 HE launch announcement)
sticks.measuredNotes: Gamepadla has no full stick test for the G7 HE, only a linearity test, so center error, circle error, asymmetry and measured bit resolution are unavailable. That linearity test (firmware 6.33, cable, XInput) measured 91.5% linearity, 4.3% tremor, 172 total positions and 0.00580 step resolution. GameSir's own marketing claim of '0 Fluctuation, 0 Deviation and 0 Circularity error' is unverified marketing language, not a measurement.

triggers.notes: No physical trigger stops or trigger locks; Windows Central calls this out as a specific omission. Hair-trigger mode is toggled by holding M + LT or M + RT for 2 seconds until the corresponding trigger vibrates. GameSir claims '100% response area'. Trigger travel distance is not documented.

controllers.dpad: Microswitch (tactile switch) d-pad, a change from the G7 SE's membrane d-pad, giving crisp clicky feedback. Doubles as headset volume and game/chat balance control when held with the M button.
controllers.faceButtons: Microswitch ABXY rated by GameSir for a 3 million press lifespan, with clicky tactile feedback. This is the headline difference from the G7 SE's membrane buttons and is a return to the original G7's design.

pollingRate.pc: 250 Hz default; 500 Hz and 1000 Hz selectable in GameSir Nexus
pollingRate.notes: GameSir states the Xbox console enforces a 250 Hz cap so 1000 Hz is PC-only, and support advises locking to 250 Hz if you use the 3.5 mm headset jack. Gamepadla verified roughly 988 Hz, 499 Hz and 250 Hz operating points on firmware 6.40. GameSir's published Windows 11 / firmware 6.30+ / Nexus 1.2.9+ prerequisites for 1000 Hz are written for the G7 and G7 SE; whether identical prerequisites apply to the HE is not separately documented.

battery.notes: Wired only. GameSir's spec sheet lists 'Battery: No' and gamepadla's verified spec list records 'No battery'. There is no battery-life claim to attribute, measured or manufacturer.

extraButtons.notes: Two rear paddles (L4/R4), a front 'M' (Mode) button below the d-pad, and a mic mute button. Unlike the G7 SE, the G7 HE has NO physical lock latches for the back buttons: GameSir's product spec list omits the 'Back Button Quick Latches' line that the SE spec list carries, Windows Central specifically flags the removal, and PCGamingWiki and comparison tables agree. Be aware GameSir's own G7 HE manual page still says 'two lockable back buttons' and even refers to 'the G7 SE' in its body text, which appears to be copy-pasted from the SE manual. Remap by holding M + R4/L4 for 3 seconds until the indicator blinks slowly, then tapping the target button.

gyro.notes: GameSir's official gyroscope list does not include the G7 HE, and gamepadla's verified specs also record no gyroscope.

controllers.rumble: Four rumble motors: one in each grip plus one behind each trigger (impulse triggers). Vibration is configurable per profile in GameSir Nexus, and impulse triggers can be forced on for all games.

faceplates.notes: Magnetic swappable faceplate with painting support. G7 series faceplates fit the newer G7 Pro, but the G7 Pro's three-part split faceplate does NOT fit the G7, G7 SE or G7 HE. Calibration must be performed with the faceplate installed or the stick range values will be wrong.

controllers.software: GameSir Nexus (Xbox and PC; a 'Legacy GameSir Nexus' build also exists). The G7 HE does not use GameSir Connect, which is the app for the G7 Pro line. One gamepadla commenter reports Nexus failing to surface the newest firmware, matching GameSir's own instruction to fall back to a standalone PC upgrader.
notableFeatures: Microswitch ABXY and microswitch d-pad rated for 3 million presses, the main upgrade over the G7 SE
Hall Effect sticks claimed at up to 5 million cycles, with anti-friction glide rings
Hall Effect analog triggers with hair-trigger toggle (hold M + LT/RT for 2 seconds)
Rubberized silicone rear grips, not present on the G7 SE
Four rumble motors including impulse triggers
Three custom profiles plus default, switched on-pad with M + Y (default), M + B (1), M + A (2), M + X (3)
3.5 mm audio jack with on-pad volume and game/chat balance via M + d-pad, plus a dedicated mic mute button
Zero-deadzone option and exclusive 'Raw' stick mode in GameSir Nexus
Magnetic swappable paint-friendly faceplate
Gamepadla measured 2.84 ms button latency at roughly 988 Hz on firmware 6.40, but notably high stick latency of 11.56 ms in the same run (versus 3.23 ms for the G7 SE)

knownIssues.symptom: Controller is connected and lit but registers no input, disconnects constantly, or will not power on.
knownIssues.cause: PID recognition failure between controller and host, or the controller sitting in the wrong input mode (XInput vs GIP).
knownIssues.fix: While connected, hold the Xbox/Home button + M button for 3 seconds (an indicator tone should sound), then unplug and replug to restore the original PID and device recognition. If that fails, hold the Xbox/Home button + Share button for 3 seconds while connected to force-switch to XInput. Also move to a rear motherboard USB port rather than a case port or hub, and swap in a verified data-capable cable.

knownIssues.symptom: Random disconnects, failure to power on, or dead inputs traced to the installed firmware.
knownIssues.cause: GameSir names firmware 6.33, 6.38 and 6.5.6 as known problematic versions for the G7 SE and G7 HE that cause connection-related issues.
knownIssues.fix: Check your version in GameSir Nexus (the 'Firmware Upgrade' arrow at top right) or Legacy GameSir Nexus ('Updates' on the controller page) and update to a current stable build. If Nexus does not offer the update, use GameSir's standalone manual upgrader for G7 HE/SE on a PC.

knownIssues.symptom: Microswitch face buttons or the d-pad double-click or send the wrong input; a bumper auto-clicks on its own.
knownIssues.cause: Corrupted mapping/profile state or outdated firmware.
knownIssues.fix: Hold the Xbox button + Menu button for 5 seconds while connected to run the function reset, then update firmware to the latest version in GameSir Nexus (GameSir's page cites V6.40 as the target at time of writing), falling back to the standalone PC upgrader if Nexus does not show it.

knownIssues.symptom: 3.5 mm headset produces no audio and the mic does not work.
knownIssues.cause: Report rates above 250 Hz disable the controller's onboard audio by design; secondary causes are an incompletely inserted headset plug or an outdated firmware build.
knownIssues.fix: GameSir support says the polling rate in GameSir Nexus on PC 'should be locked at 250hz to avoid potential problems'. Push the headset plug fully flush, confirm the mic is not muted (red LED near the bottom of the pad, or double-tap M to toggle), and on Xbox set Settings > General > Volume & audio output > Headset audio to 'Stereo uncompressed'. If it persists after a firmware update, test a different CTIA-standard headset.

knownIssues.symptom: Sticks appear to drift straight out of the box after the initial deadzone is set to 0 in GameSir Nexus.
knownIssues.cause: Not hardware drift. Zero deadzone is a true physical zero, making the stick hypersensitive to residual movement.
knownIssues.fix: GameSir's official answer is to set the initial deadzone to roughly 3-5 rather than 0. For genuine stick or trigger faults, run the manual Stick & Trigger Calibration and the function reset (Xbox + Menu held 5 seconds).

knownIssues.symptom: Controller becomes unresponsive or refuses to power on after a button combo was held while the cable was inserted.
knownIssues.cause: Holding Xbox + Menu, or View + Xbox + Menu, WHILE plugging in enters DFU (firmware update) mode or manual calibration mode instead of normal operation. GameSir also warns that cable guards can make a half-seated cable feel fully inserted.
knownIssues.fix: Unplug, reinsert the cable firmly with no buttons held until it clicks, then hold the Xbox button to power on. If still unresponsive, perform a manual firmware upgrade from a Windows PC using GameSir's standalone G7 series upgrader.

knownIssues.symptom: Back buttons are pressed accidentally during normal play.
knownIssues.cause: The G7 HE removed the two physical quick-latch lock switches that the G7 SE has on its back buttons, so the paddles cannot be mechanically disabled.
knownIssues.fix: No hardware workaround exists. Clear the mapping instead: hold M + R4 (or M + L4) for 3 seconds until the indicator blinks slowly, then tap R4 (or L4) itself to cancel its assigned value, or use a profile with the back buttons unmapped.

faq.q: What is the correct stick and trigger calibration procedure for the G7 HE? (Do NOT use the G7 Pro procedure.)
faq.a: 1) Hold View + Menu + Xbox buttons and, while still holding, insert the USB-C cable into your PC's USB port; release after plugging in. The indicator blinks slowly in white. 2) Without touching LT, RT or either stick, press A. The indicator goes out. 3) Press LT and RT to maximum travel and rotate both sticks at maximum angle three times, then press A. The indicator turns solid white to confirm completion. 4) Unplug and replug before using. Caveats: calibration must be performed with the faceplate installed or range values will be incorrect; move at a steady, gentle speed; manual calibration often works when in-app calibration fails; calibration applies only to analog trigger mode. CRITICAL: this hold-while-plugging-in procedure belongs to the older G7 series (G7 / G7 SE / G7 HE). GameSir explicitly warns that applying this older-G7 calibration procedure to a G7 Pro will put that controller into firmware update mode and leave it unable to power on normally. The G7 Pro instead uses View + Menu + Home held 2 seconds while already connected.

faq.q: What exactly is different between the G7 HE and the G7 SE?
faq.a: Both are wired-only, share the same 152 x 103 x 63 mm shell, the same GameSir Hall Effect sticks and Hall Effect analog triggers, the same four rumble motors, the same two back buttons, the same 3.5 mm jack and mute button, the same magnetic faceplate, and the same GameSir Nexus software. The differences: the HE uses microswitch ABXY and a microswitch d-pad (3 million press rating) where the SE uses membrane; the HE adds rubberized silicone grips; the HE removes the SE's two physical back-button lock latches; the HE weighs 227 g versus the SE's 221 g; and the HE is $49.99 versus the SE's $44.99. GameSir's own comparison FAQ answer is published only as an image with no text, so this comparison is assembled from the two product spec sheets plus PCGamingWiki and Windows Central.

faq.q: Is the G7 HE wireless, and does it have a battery?
faq.a: No. It is wired only, using a 3 m detachable USB-C cable, and GameSir's spec sheet lists 'Battery: No'. There is nothing to charge and no battery-life figure of any kind. Windows Central's main criticism of the controller is precisely that it remains wired at a $49.99 price in 2024.

faq.q: How do I reset the G7 HE to default settings?
faq.a: Function reset: hold the Xbox button + Menu button for 5 seconds while connected. This is also GameSir's documented fix for a key bind you set incorrectly in Nexus and cannot undo, and for buttons registering double or wrong inputs. Full reset: hold View + Menu + M until the logo button blinks, then hold the Xbox button for 3 seconds, which resets the profile and all controller settings. You can also simply reapply the default profile with M + Y.

faq.q: How do I enable hair-trigger mode, switch profiles, and remap the back buttons?
faq.a: Hair trigger: hold M + LT or M + RT for 2 seconds until the corresponding trigger vibrates. Profiles: M + Y for default, M + B for Profile 1, M + A for Profile 2, M + X for Profile 3. Back buttons: hold M + R4 or M + L4 for 3 seconds until the indicator blinks slowly, then tap the button you want assigned; the indicator turns solid to confirm. To cancel, repeat the combo and tap R4/L4 itself.

faq.q: How do I control headset volume and the game/chat mix from the controller?
faq.a: A headset must be plugged into the 3.5 mm jack. Hold M + d-pad Up/Down to raise or lower master volume; the G7 HE connection tutorial documents 11 levels while the manual says 10, with a beep at maximum and minimum. Hold M + d-pad Left/Right to shift the balance between game volume and voice chat volume, with a beep at maximum, middle and minimum. Press the mic mute button to mute (indicator turns solid red) and press again to unmute; holding it while muted temporarily unmutes.

faq.q: Can the G7 HE reach 1000 Hz polling on an Xbox console?
faq.a: No. GameSir states the Xbox console enforces a 250 Hz polling rate limit, so the 1000 Hz option is only available on PC. GameSir additionally warns that any polling rate above 250 Hz disables the onboard 3.5 mm audio, and support recommends locking to 250 Hz if you use a headset through the controller.

faq.q: Does the G7 HE have a gyroscope or trigger stops?
faq.a: Neither. GameSir's official gyro-equipped Xbox controller list covers the G7 Pro, G7 Pro Wuchang, G7 Pro Zenless Zone Zero, Tarantula Pro Xbox and T7 Pro Sugar Whirl, and the G7 HE is not among them; gamepadla's verified specs also record no gyroscope and no trigger lock. Windows Central lists the absence of trigger stops as a notable omission for FPS players.

faq.q: What can I configure in GameSir Nexus for the G7 HE?
faq.a: Three controller profiles covering button mapping, stick and trigger fine-tuning, vibration and more. For sticks: stick curves, initial and max deadzone, anti-deadzone, a true zero deadzone option, and a switch between Default and GameSir's exclusive 'Raw' mode. For triggers: impulse triggers for all games, hair trigger in Static mode (any movement in range reads as a full 100% pull) or Adaptive mode (100% on entering the range, instantly dropping to 0 on minimal release), and a Continuous Trigger toggle that holds an input until pressed again. Firmware updates also run through Nexus, with a standalone PC upgrader as a fallback.

controllers.name: GameSir G7 Pro
controllers.tagline: Xbox-licensed tri-mode controller with Mag-Res TMR sticks, microswitch face buttons and 1000 Hz polling on PC.

connectivity.notes: Connection support is platform-dependent: wired only for Xbox consoles, wired or 2.4 GHz for PC, Bluetooth 5.3 for Android.

sticks.measuredNotes: Measured values vary substantially by connection mode. gamepadla recorded center error between 1.2% and 3.1% and stick resolution between 13.7-bit (13,107 steps) and 8-bit (256 steps) depending on the mode tested. The controller applies no inner deadzone, so its natural center error is not masked in software.

triggers.notes: Microswitch trigger stops allow switching from analog travel to a short mouse-click style actuation.

controllers.dpad: Mechanical microswitch, three selectable D-pad configurations

pollingRate.notes: Xbox consoles enforce a 250 Hz cap, so 1000 Hz is a PC-only capability. Reaching 1000 Hz on PC requires the controller to switch from GIP to XInput mode.

battery.notes: Charges over USB-C or via the optional charging station. Battery indicator flashes red below 15%.

extraButtons.notes: Four extra inputs (L4, L5, R4, R5) ship as null inputs and do nothing until mapped.

gyro.notes: PC only. Can be mapped to stick, buttons or mouse via GameSir Nexus.

controllers.rumble: Four motors — one in each grip and one in each trigger

faceplates.notes: Three-part magnetic faceplate, backward compatible with earlier G7 series faceplates.

notableFeatures: Mag-Res TMR sticks with no applied inner deadzone
Raw and Circular stick trajectory modes
Hall Effect analog triggers with microswitch stops
Three-part magnetic swappable faceplate
Built-in gyro with mouse mapping (PC only)
Four remappable rear inputs

knownIssues.symptom: Sticks appear to drift even though the controller is nearly new
knownIssues.cause: TMR sticks are magnetic and do not wear like potentiometers, so this is rarely mechanical. The G7 Pro applies no inner deadzone, so its natural center error is visible to games. A misconfigured anti-deadzone in Nexus can also produce it — GameSir's own documentation states improper anti-deadzone configuration 'may appear similar to stick drift'.
knownIssues.fix: Set Anti-deadzone Initial back to 0 in Nexus, confirm you are not in Raw (zero deadzone) trajectory mode, recalibrate, then add a small Initial deadzone only if needed.

knownIssues.symptom: Stick ranges are wrong or inconsistent after calibration
knownIssues.cause: Calibration performed with the magnetic faceplate removed.
knownIssues.fix: GameSir documentation states calibration must be performed with the faceplate installed; calibrating without it produces incorrect range values. Reinstall the faceplate and recalibrate.

knownIssues.symptom: Sticks feel too fast or too twitchy after calibrating
knownIssues.cause: Rotation speed during calibration affects the resulting sensitivity.
knownIssues.fix: Recalibrate using slow, steady, gentle full rotations. GameSir notes faster rotation during calibration yields higher sensitivity than slower rotation.

knownIssues.symptom: Controller shows in Windows as 'Xbox 360 Controller' and disconnects when GameSir Nexus is closed
knownIssues.cause: Expected behaviour. 1000 Hz polling and keyboard/mouse bindings require the controller to switch protocol from GIP (Xbox Gaming Device) to XInput, which renames the device and forces a brief reconnect.
knownIssues.fix: This is not a fault. The mode can be switched manually by holding Xbox + Share for about 3 seconds.

knownIssues.symptom: Controller is powered on and connected but invisible to games and to GameSir Nexus
knownIssues.cause: The controller is stuck in HID (Android support) mode.
knownIssues.fix: Hold Xbox + Mode for roughly 4 seconds until the Xbox indicator blinks twice to reset the PID. Alternatively hold Share + Menu for about 4 seconds to toggle the mode.

knownIssues.symptom: Controller will not power on after attempting calibration found in an older guide or video
knownIssues.cause: The calibration procedure for the older G7 / G7 SE / G7 HE puts a G7 Pro into firmware update mode instead of calibration mode.
knownIssues.fix: Do not use the older G7 sequence. Use View + Xbox + Menu on the G7 Pro. If the controller is already stuck, GameSir directs users to perform a manual firmware upgrade from a Windows PC.

knownIssues.symptom: Set polling to 1000 Hz but measured rate is lower
knownIssues.cause: The controller has not completed the switch into XInput mode, or the USB path cannot sustain the rate.
knownIssues.fix: Fully close Nexus to trigger the mode switch, or hold Xbox + Share for 3 seconds to force it. Prefer rear motherboard USB ports over front-panel ports and hubs, and use a known data-capable cable. Two indicator blinks mean the mode swap failed.

faq.q: How do I calibrate the sticks and triggers?
faq.a: With the faceplate installed and the controller connected, hold View + Xbox + Menu until the Xbox indicator flashes slowly white. Without touching the sticks or triggers, press A — the indicator turns off. Then pull LT and RT to full travel three times and rotate both sticks at full extent three times, and press A. A solid white indicator confirms completion. Rotate slowly and steadily. Calibration affects analog trigger mode only, not mouse-click mode.

faq.q: How do I reset all profiles and settings?
faq.a: Hold View + Mode + Menu. The Xbox LED blinks three times to confirm all profiles and custom settings have been cleared. Individual profiles can also be reset from within GameSir Nexus.

faq.q: How do I map the rear buttons and mini bumpers?
faq.a: They are null inputs with no default function. Hold Mode + the remappable button until the indicator blinks, then press the target button to assign it. To clear a mapping, repeat and press the same remappable button again. They can also be configured in GameSir Nexus.

faq.q: Which app does the G7 Pro use?
faq.a: GameSir Nexus, available from the Xbox and Windows stores. Note that the G7 Pro 8K PC uses GameSir Connect instead — the two apps do not cover each other's hardware.

faq.q: Can I get 1000 Hz on an Xbox console?
faq.a: No. Xbox consoles enforce a 250 Hz polling limit, so the 1000 Hz option is available on PC only.

faq.q: How do I switch preset profiles?
faq.a: Mode + Y selects configuration 1, Mode + B selects 2, Mode + A selects 3, Mode + X selects 4.

faq.q: How do I enable hair trigger mode?
faq.a: Hold Mode + LT or RT for 2 seconds to toggle hair trigger mode on or off.

faq.q: The gyro is behaving incorrectly. How do I recalibrate it?
faq.a: Place the controller flat on a level surface and hold Mode + Share for 3 seconds. The logo LED flashes orange and white alternately during calibration.

controllers.name: GameSir G7 Pro 8K
controllers.tagline: PC-focused variant with Gen-2 TMR sticks and an 8000 Hz polling rate, managed by GameSir Connect rather than Nexus.

connectivity.notes: GameSir documents wired and 2.4 GHz as the supported PC connection paths for this model. Bluetooth is not the documented PC detection path.

sticks.measuredNotes: Figures measured on the Aimlabs Edition. A second tested mode recorded 3.2% / 2.8%. As with the base G7 Pro, no inner deadzone is applied, so natural center error is exposed to games.

pollingRate.notes: GameSir advises reverting to 250 Hz when troubleshooting, since a raised polling rate can introduce unrelated problems.

extraButtons.notes: XInput hides the gyro, rear paddles and extra bumpers; mode choice affects which extras are exposed.

gyro.notes: Not exposed in plain XInput mode.

notableFeatures: 8000 Hz polling over both wired and 2.4 GHz
Gen-2 TMR sticks with lower power draw than Gen-1
Per-stick deadzone toggle
Raw (zero deadzone) and Circular trajectory modes
3.5 mm audio over both wired and 2.4 GHz

knownIssues.symptom: Controller never appears in GameSir Nexus
knownIssues.cause: The G7 Pro 8K PC is not a Nexus device. GameSir has stated publicly that it does not work with Nexus, which is intended for its Xbox-licensed controllers.
knownIssues.fix: Use GameSir Connect instead. Nexus not listing the controller is expected behaviour, not a fault. Connect also requires the controller to be in XInput mode via cable or dongle to list it.

knownIssues.symptom: Gyro, rear paddles or extra bumpers do nothing in a game
knownIssues.cause: Plain XInput does not expose those inputs.
knownIssues.fix: Choose the connection mode that exposes what you need rather than looking for a single setting, or clone the inputs onto standard buttons in GameSir Connect.

knownIssues.symptom: Intermittent disconnects or odd behaviour after raising the polling rate
knownIssues.cause: High polling rates can conflict with some USB paths and software.
knownIssues.fix: Set the polling rate back to 250 Hz to confirm, then raise it again. Prefer rear motherboard USB ports and avoid hubs.

knownIssues.symptom: Sticks or triggers reading incorrectly
knownIssues.cause: Calibration data is off.
knownIssues.fix: Calibrate from the app via the Test icon with Mode + Menu, or manually: hold View + Home + Menu until the Home indicator flashes slowly white, press A with nothing touched, then pull both triggers fully three times and rotate both sticks fully three times and press A.

faq.q: Which app manages the G7 Pro 8K?
faq.a: GameSir Connect. This is the single most common source of confusion with this model — Nexus is for GameSir's Xbox-licensed controllers and will not list the 8K. Per GameSir's own downloads page, Connect covers the G7 Pro 8K PC editions (Aimlabs, Champion, Nioh 3, Royal2), Tarantula 8K PC, Tegenaria Lite, Super Nova, Nova Lite 2 and Cyclone 2.

faq.q: Does it really reach 8000 Hz on wireless?
faq.a: GameSir states 8000 Hz is supported on both wired and 2.4 GHz. Independent measurement of the Aimlabs Edition recorded a median around 7936 Hz on both cable and dongle.

faq.q: How do I toggle the stick deadzone?
faq.a: Hold the M button and press in the left or right stick for 2 seconds to toggle that stick's deadzone on or off.

faq.q: How do I enable zero-deadzone (Raw) mode?
faq.a: Hold the Mode button and press in the left or right stick until the controller vibrates. This toggles between Raw mode (zero deadzone) and Circular stick trajectory.

faq.q: Does it support 3.5 mm audio wirelessly?
faq.a: Yes — GameSir states 3.5 mm audio output works over both wired and 2.4 GHz connections.

controllers.name: GameSir G7 SE
controllers.tagline: Officially Xbox-licensed wired controller and the first Xbox controller with Hall Effect sticks, using membrane face buttons and lockable back buttons.

connectivity.notes: Wired only, via a 3 m detachable USB-C (USB-A to USB-C) cable. No battery and no wireless mode of any kind. GameSir's manual tech-spec block also lists Android, but the FAQ and product page list only Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One and Windows 10/11, so Android support is unconfirmed.

sticks.measuredNotes: Center error measured by gamepadla on firmware 6.5.6, single unit. GameSir publishes no cycle-life rating for the G7 SE sticks; the 5-million-cycle figure applies to the G7 HE only. Gamepadla also measured 0.0% circle error on both sticks, 4.6%/6.9% asymmetry, no inner deadzone, 0.6 mm outer deadzone, and no cardinal snapping.

triggers.notes: No physical trigger stops or trigger locks. A software/hardware hair-trigger mode is toggled by holding M + LT or M + RT for 2 seconds until the controller vibrates. GameSir claims '100% response area'. Trigger travel distance is not documented.

controllers.dpad: Membrane (rubber-dome) 8-way d-pad, described by reviewers as soft compared with the microswitch d-pad on the G7 and G7 HE. Doubles as headset volume and game/chat balance control when held with the M button. D-pad diagonal sensitivity is adjustable in GameSir Nexus.
controllers.faceButtons: Membrane ABXY. No manufacturer-published press-lifespan rating. The original G7 used microswitches, the SE dropped them, and the G7 HE reinstated them.

pollingRate.pc: 250 Hz default; 500 Hz and 1000 Hz selectable in GameSir Nexus
pollingRate.notes: GameSir states the Xbox console enforces a 250 Hz cap, so 1000 Hz is a PC-only option. Per GameSir's help center, 500 Hz requires Windows 10 or newer, while 1000 Hz requires Windows 11, firmware 6.30 or higher, GameSir Nexus 1.2.9 or higher, and a reboot after first enabling it. Both 500 Hz and 1000 Hz disable the 3.5 mm headphone jack. Gamepadla measured a genuine 1000 Hz median (1000.29 Hz average) on firmware 6.6.4, though some community reports claim units cap near 500 Hz.

battery.notes: Wired only. GameSir's spec sheet lists 'Battery: No' and gamepadla's verified spec list records 'No battery'. There is nothing to charge and no battery-life claim to attribute.

extraButtons.notes: Two rear paddles labelled L4 and R4, plus a front 'M' (Mode) button below the d-pad and a dedicated mic mute button. Each back button has a physical quick-latch slider that mechanically locks it out to prevent accidental presses. Remap on the fly: hold M + L4 or M + R4 for 3 seconds until the indicator blinks slowly, then tap the button you want to assign. Repeat and tap L4/R4 itself to clear the assignment.

gyro.notes: GameSir's official gyroscope list names G7 Pro, G7 Pro Wuchang, G7 Pro Zenless Zone Zero, Tarantula Pro Xbox and T7 Pro Sugar Whirl among Xbox controllers. The G7 SE is not on that list, and gamepadla's verified specs also record no gyroscope.

controllers.rumble: Four rumble motors: one in each grip plus one behind each trigger (impulse triggers). Vibration strength is configurable per profile in GameSir Nexus, and impulse triggers can be forced on for all games.

faceplates.notes: Magnetic swappable faceplate designed to accept paint. Faceplates are one of the few parts GameSir sells separately. G7 series faceplates fit the newer G7 Pro, but the G7 Pro's 3-part split faceplate does NOT fit the G7, G7 SE or G7 HE. Calibration must be performed with the faceplate installed or the stick range values will be wrong.

controllers.software: GameSir Nexus (available on both Xbox and PC via the Microsoft Store; a 'Legacy GameSir Nexus' build also exists). The G7 SE does not use GameSir Connect, which is the app for the G7 Pro line.
notableFeatures: First Xbox-licensed controller with Hall Effect sticks (launched June 2023)
Hall Effect analog triggers with a hair-trigger toggle (hold M + LT/RT for 2 seconds)
Two remappable back buttons with physical lock latches, remappable without software
Four rumble motors including impulse triggers
Three custom profiles plus default, switched on-pad with M + Y (default), M + B (1), M + A (2), M + X (3)
3.5 mm audio jack with on-pad volume and game/chat balance via M + d-pad, plus a dedicated mic mute button
Zero-deadzone option and an exclusive 'Raw' stick mode in GameSir Nexus
Magnetic paint-friendly swappable faceplate
Gamepadla measured 3.00 ms button and 3.23 ms stick latency at 1000 Hz on firmware 6.6.4

knownIssues.symptom: Controller is plugged in and the light is on, but no inputs register, or it repeatedly disconnects, or it will not power on at all.
knownIssues.cause: PID recognition failure between the controller and host, or the controller being in the wrong input mode (XInput vs GIP).
knownIssues.fix: While connected, hold the Xbox button + M button for 3 seconds (you should hear an indicator tone), then unplug and replug to switch back to the original PID and restore device recognition. If that fails, hold the Xbox button + Share button for 3 seconds while connected to force-switch between XInput and GIP modes. Also try motherboard-rear USB ports rather than case ports or hubs, and a known-good data cable.

knownIssues.symptom: Connection instability: random disconnects, failure to power on, or no input, on specific firmware builds.
knownIssues.cause: GameSir names firmware 6.33, 6.38 and 6.5.6 as known problematic versions for the G7 SE and G7 HE that cause connection-related issues.
knownIssues.fix: Check your version in GameSir Nexus (the upward arrow labelled 'Firmware Upgrade' at top right) or in Legacy GameSir Nexus (the 'Updates' button on the controller page), then update to a current stable build. If Nexus does not offer the update, GameSir provides a standalone manual upgrader for G7 SE/HE on PC.

knownIssues.symptom: The 3.5 mm headset jack goes completely dead: no game audio and no mic.
knownIssues.cause: Selecting a 500 Hz or 1000 Hz report rate disables the controller's onboard audio. This is by design, not a fault.
knownIssues.fix: Set the report rate back to 250 Hz in GameSir Nexus on PC. GameSir support explicitly says the polling rate 'should be locked at 250hz to avoid potential problems' for headset use. Also ensure the headset is pushed fully flush into the jack, and on Xbox set Settings > General > Volume & audio output > Headset audio to 'Stereo uncompressed'.

knownIssues.symptom: The sticks appear to drift immediately out of the box after setting the initial deadzone to 0 in GameSir Nexus.
knownIssues.cause: Not hardware drift. A 0 deadzone is a true physical zero, which makes the stick extremely sensitive to the smallest residual movement.
knownIssues.fix: GameSir's official answer: set the initial deadzone to roughly 3-5 instead of 0 and behaviour returns to normal.

knownIssues.symptom: Face buttons or the d-pad double-click or register the wrong input; a bumper auto-clicks by itself.
knownIssues.cause: Corrupted profile/mapping state or outdated firmware.
knownIssues.fix: Run the function reset by holding the Xbox button + Menu button for 5 seconds while the controller is connected, then update the firmware to the latest version in GameSir Nexus (GameSir's page cites V6.40 as the target at the time of writing), using the standalone PC upgrader if Nexus does not offer it.

knownIssues.symptom: The controller becomes unresponsive or refuses to power on after a button combination was held while plugging in the USB cable.
knownIssues.cause: Holding Xbox + Menu, or View + Xbox + Menu, WHILE plugging in the cable puts the controller into DFU (firmware update) mode or manual calibration mode rather than normal operation. GameSir also notes that controllers with cable guards can feel fully seated when only half inserted.
knownIssues.fix: Unplug, plug the cable in firmly with no buttons held until it audibly clicks, then hold the Xbox button to power on. If it stays unresponsive, perform a manual firmware upgrade from a Windows PC using GameSir's standalone G7 series upgrader package.

knownIssues.symptom: Controller works perfectly on PC but is not detected by the Xbox console at all.
knownIssues.cause: Stale console state / cached USB enumeration.
knownIssues.fix: Full power cycle: plug the controller into the console's rear USB port, hold the console power button for 10+ seconds until it fully shuts down, unplug the power cord for about 30 seconds, press the console power button 10 times to discharge residual power, then power back on with the controller still in the rear port.

faq.q: What is the correct stick and trigger calibration procedure for the G7 SE? (Do NOT use the G7 Pro procedure.)
faq.a: 1) Hold View + Menu + Xbox buttons and, while still holding them, insert the USB-C cable into your PC's USB port; release after plugging in. The indicator blinks slowly in white. 2) Without touching the triggers or sticks, press A. The indicator goes out. 3) Press LT and RT to their maximum travel and rotate both sticks at maximum angle three times, then press A. The indicator turns solid white to confirm. 4) Unplug and replug the controller before use. Important caveats: calibration must be done with the faceplate installed or the range values will be wrong; move at a steady, gentle speed to avoid data-collection errors; manual calibration often succeeds when the in-app calibration fails. CRITICAL: this hold-while-plugging-in procedure is specific to the older G7 series (G7 / G7 SE / G7 HE). GameSir explicitly warns that using this older-G7 calibration procedure on a G7 Pro will put that controller into firmware update mode and leave it unable to power on normally. The G7 Pro instead uses View + Menu + Home held for 2 seconds while already connected.

faq.q: How do I reset the G7 SE to default settings?
faq.a: Two documented options. Function reset: hold the Xbox button + Menu button for 5 seconds while connected, which also fixes bad key binds you cannot undo. Full profile/settings reset: hold View + Menu + M until the logo button blinks, then hold the Xbox button for 3 seconds; this resets the profile and all controller settings. You can also just reapply the default profile with M + Y.

faq.q: Is the G7 SE wireless, and does it have a battery?
faq.a: No. It is wired only, using a 3 m detachable USB-C cable, and it has no battery at all. GameSir's own spec sheet lists 'Battery: No', so there is no charge time or battery-life figure for this controller.

faq.q: How do I get 1000 Hz polling, and why does my headset stop working when I do?
faq.a: 1000 Hz is PC-only; GameSir states the Xbox console enforces a 250 Hz cap. On PC you need Windows 11, G7 SE firmware 6.30 or higher, and GameSir Nexus 1.2.9 or higher; select the report rate under Profiles and restart the computer the first time. 500 Hz works on Windows 10 or higher and needs no script. Running either 500 Hz or 1000 Hz disables the controller's headphone jack, which is expected behaviour. GameSir recommends 500 Hz for general use and 1000 Hz for competitive play.

faq.q: How do I remap the back buttons and switch profiles without software?
faq.a: Remap: hold M + R4 (or M + L4) for 3 seconds until the indicator blinks slowly, then tap the button you want mapped to it; the indicator turns solid to confirm. Clear it: repeat the combo and tap R4/L4 itself. Profiles: M + Y is the default profile, M + B is Profile 1, M + A is Profile 2, M + X is Profile 3. The two quick-latch sliders on the back mechanically enable or disable the back buttons entirely.

faq.q: How do I enable hair-trigger mode and control headset volume from the pad?
faq.a: Hair trigger: hold M + LT or M + RT for 2 seconds until the controller vibrates; repeat to disable. Master volume: hold M + d-pad Up/Down (10 levels, with a beep at max and min). Game/chat balance: hold M + d-pad Left/Right (beeps at max, middle and min). A headset must be plugged into the 3.5 mm jack for volume control to do anything. The mic mute button turns the indicator red when muted; holding it temporarily unmutes.

faq.q: What software does the G7 SE use, and what can it change?
faq.a: GameSir Nexus, available on both Xbox and PC. It supports three custom profiles covering button mapping, d-pad diagonal tuning, stick and trigger fine-tuning (including stick curves, initial/max deadzone, anti-deadzone, hair-trigger static vs adaptive modes, and continuous trigger toggle), vibration configuration, report rate selection, and firmware updates. Sticks can be set to zero deadzone and switched between Default and GameSir's exclusive 'Raw' mode. Note the G7 SE uses Nexus, not GameSir Connect, which is the app for the G7 Pro family.

faq.q: Does the G7 SE have a gyroscope?
faq.a: No. GameSir's official gyro-equipped list covers the G7 Pro, G7 Pro Wuchang, G7 Pro Zenless Zone Zero, Tarantula Pro Xbox and T7 Pro Sugar Whirl on the Xbox side. The G7 SE is not included, and gamepadla's verified spec sheet also records no gyroscope.

faq.q: Are G7 Pro faceplates compatible with the G7 SE?
faq.a: No, not in that direction. The G7 Pro can accept faceplates from the older G7 series, but the G7 Pro's three-part split faceplate is not compatible with the G7, G7 SE or G7 HE. Magnetic faceplates for the G7 series are one of the few parts GameSir sells separately; internal components, buttons and USB ports are not sold as spares.

controllers.name: GameSir Super Nova
controllers.tagline: A $49.99 tri-mode multiplatform controller with Hall Effect sticks and triggers, magnetic swappable faceplates, and an auto start-stop charging dock.

connectivity.notes: Tri-mode: USB-C wired, 2.4GHz dongle, Bluetooth 5.0. A three-position rear mode switch selects 2.4G / Off / Bluetooth. Does NOT support Xbox consoles. GameSir's own manual lists platforms as 'PC, Switch, and Android' while the product page and retail listings add iOS; Switch 2 support is claimed on retail listings. Bluetooth connects to PC only as a DS4 device, which is why GameSir Connect cannot see it over Bluetooth.

sticks.tech: GameSir Hall Effect (non-contact magnetic), with anti-friction glide rings — NOT TMR
sticks.durability: Up to 5 million cycles (GameSir manufacturer claim)
sticks.measuredCenterError: 0.0-2.3% left / 0.0-2.7% right across four test runs
sticks.measuredResolution: 8.0-bit, ~256 steps (gamepadla, dongle in DS4 mode, FW 1.0.6) — likely reflects the reporting mode rather than the sensor ceiling
sticks.measuredNotes: Four gamepadla Stick Tracer runs on firmware 1.0.6 produced center errors from 0.0% to 2.3% on the left stick and 0.0% to 2.7% on the right. The 0.0% results were attributed to the controller's built-in inner deadzone masking the true figure. Unlike the G7 Pro family, the Super Nova does apply an inner deadzone, which is why apparent drift is less common on it.

triggers.tech: Hall Effect analog triggers with a 100% response area
triggers.notes: A physical trigger gear switch selects long-pull or short-pull position. After switching, GameSir instructs you to press the trigger fully three times so it auto-calibrates the new pull distance. Hair trigger mode is a separate software toggle: hold M + LT/RT, and it requires the trigger to be set to the long-pull position first.

controllers.dpad: Membrane D-pad. TechRadar's review specifically calls the D-pad the weakest part of the controller ('isn't best in class').
controllers.faceButtons: Membrane ABXY, marketed as noise-free/silent. The ABXY buttons are physically detachable so the layout can be rearranged between Xbox and Nintendo positions by hand. Button VALUES can be swapped separately in firmware by holding M + the south face button, which swaps A-B and X-Y.

pollingRate.notes: Xbox consoles are not supported. Bluetooth is 125 Hz. Gamepadla measured 996-1000 Hz median wired, 999-1000 Hz via dongle, and 125-391 Hz over Bluetooth; measured button latency was 7.32 ms wired (XInput), 12.1-20.4 ms via dongle, and 14.5-26.9 ms over Bluetooth (GPDL method, firmware 1.0.6/1.3). Note that connecting by cable while in Switch mode drops polling to 125 Hz.

battery.claimedLife: Manufacturer estimate of about 15 hours. GameSir publishes no battery-life figure on its product page or manual; TechRadar states that GameSir supplied the 15-hour figure on request.
battery.notes: Third-party review estimates vary widely and are less reliable: roughly 16 hours at 50% RGB brightness and up to ~20 hours with RGB off (Techxreviews); some reseller spec tables claim 'up to 25 hours,' which is not supported by GameSir's own 15-hour estimate. There is no battery percentage readout in the software or on the controller — the only indicator is the Home light flashing red below 15%. Ships with a smart auto start-stop charging dock; lifting the controller can be set to power it on.

extraButtons.notes: Two rear buttons (L4/R4) supporting single-button mapping and macro recording, plus an M (mode/macro) button. The rear buttons ship as 'null inputs' with no function until mapped. On-controller mapping: hold M + L4/R4 until the corresponding RGB strip slowly flashes white, press the button to assign, then press L4/R4 again to save. Exiting without pressing a target button clears the assignment.

gyro.notes: Built-in 6-axis gyroscope. Calibrated on-device by placing the controller on a flat surface and holding M + Screenshot for 2 seconds; the Home light flashes red and blue alternately during the process.

controllers.rumble: Two rumble motors, one in each grip, described by GameSir as dual asymmetric motors. Vibration intensity is adjustable on the fly by holding M and pressing - or +.

faceplates.notes: Magnetic detachable middle faceplate, sold in additional colors by GameSir. The ABXY buttons themselves are also detachable for layout rearrangement. Thin RGB light strips on the front sync with a matching strip on the charging dock.

controllers.software: GameSir Connect (PC) and the GameSir app (mobile). Note that GameSir's own Super Nova manual page contains an error telling users to configure the rear buttons via GameSir Nexus — Nexus does not support this model.
notableFeatures: Hall Effect sticks AND Hall Effect triggers at a $49.99 price point
Magnetic detachable middle faceplate plus physically detachable, rearrangeable ABXY buttons
Smart auto start-stop charging dock included, with RGB that syncs to the controller
1000 Hz polling over both wired and 2.4GHz connections
Trigger gear for long/short pull plus a separate software hair-trigger mode
Extensive on-controller configuration via M-button combos (turbo, deadzone, vibration intensity, RGB, layout swap) with no software required
Membrane ABXY marketed as noise-free/silent
Rubber-coated textured grips

knownIssues.symptom: GameSir Connect cannot see the Super Nova when it is connected over Bluetooth.
knownIssues.cause: By design. Over Bluetooth the Super Nova presents to a PC only as a DS4 device, which GameSir Connect cannot access.
knownIssues.fix: Connect by cable or 2.4GHz dongle in XInput mode instead. Bluetooth cannot be used with GameSir Connect at all.

knownIssues.symptom: The Super Nova appears in GameSir Connect's device list but still will not connect, even on wired or dongle mode.
knownIssues.cause: The controller is in the wrong input mode, has the wrong USB PID selected, or a stale Windows driver is bound to it.
knownIssues.fix: GameSir's documented sequence: (1) press [-] + [+] for 3 seconds to cycle to XInput mode — indicator lights 2 and 4 illuminate; (2) press M + Home for 3 seconds to switch PID; (3) press Logo + [+] for 5 seconds to force XInput mode; (4) uninstall the driver in Device Manager and scan for hardware changes.

knownIssues.symptom: The controller soft-locks and will not power on or off after pressing 'update firmware' in GameSir Connect.
knownIssues.cause: A known bug in the firmware update flow, reported for both the Super Nova and Cyclone 2.
knownIssues.fix: Press the recessed Reset button inside the circular hole on the back of the controller using a paperclip-sized object to force it off. A separate settings/profile reset is done by holding Home + Menu until the Logo button blinks. Firmware can also be updated with GameSir's standalone manual updater: connect via USB, hold Home + X + Y for 3 seconds to enter update mode, then click update firmware.

knownIssues.symptom: Buttons fire repeatedly from a single press and the indicator light flashes red.
knownIssues.cause: Turbo (rapid-fire) mode has been enabled accidentally, usually by an M-button combo.
knownIssues.fix: Double-press the M button to clear all turbo settings. Turbo is toggled per-button by holding M and pressing A/B/X/Y/LB/RB/LT/RT.

knownIssues.symptom: The trigger lock is enabled but the trigger does not reach 100% output.
knownIssues.cause: GameSir states the trigger lock function is firmware-controlled and may not register the physical switch position on the first attempt.
knownIssues.fix: Toggle the trigger gear switch several times until the controller registers the setting. GameSir separately instructs pressing the trigger fully down three times after switching so the pull distance auto-calibrates.

knownIssues.symptom: The rear buttons do nothing at all when pressed.
knownIssues.cause: Not a fault. The rear extra buttons ship as 'null inputs' with no assigned function until they are remapped.
knownIssues.fix: Map them via GameSir Connect, the GameSir mobile app, or on-controller: hold M + L4/R4 until the RGB strip flashes white, press the target button, then press L4/R4 again to save. To clear a mapping, press the same rear button again instead of a target. Note GameSir's manual page incorrectly names 'GameSir Nexus' here — Nexus does not support the Super Nova.

knownIssues.symptom: GameSir Connect is installed but does not detect the controller, and the app never updates itself.
knownIssues.cause: A Microsoft Store glitch prevents GameSir Connect from receiving automatic updates, leaving users on a version that predates Super Nova support.
knownIssues.fix: Uninstall and reinstall GameSir Connect from the Microsoft Store, or download it directly from GameSir's software page instead of relying on Store updates.

faq.q: Which app should I use — GameSir Connect, the GameSir app, or GameSir Nexus?
faq.a: GameSir Connect on PC, or the GameSir app on mobile. GameSir Nexus does not support the Super Nova (it is for GameSir's Xbox-licensed controllers). Connect requires a wired or dongle connection in XInput mode; it cannot reach the controller over Bluetooth.

faq.q: How do I pair the Super Nova to a Nintendo Switch?
faq.a: On the Switch home screen open Controllers, then Change Grip/Order, and leave that page open. Set the rear mode switch to Bluetooth and press Home to power on. Hold Home + Y for 2 seconds until the channel indicator flashes up and down rapidly, then wait for the connection. If it fails, hold Home + Screenshot to force pairing mode and retry.

faq.q: What are the Bluetooth mode combos for each platform?
faq.a: With the mode switch in the Bluetooth position: Home + B for 2 seconds selects PC/other-device mode (appears as 'Wireless Controller'), Home + Y selects Switch mode, and Home + A selects Android mode (appears as 'GameSir-Nova Pro'). Home + Screenshot held 2-3 seconds forces pairing mode from any of these.

faq.q: How do I calibrate the sticks and triggers?
faq.a: Set the triggers to long-travel mode first. Hold [-] + [+] + Home for 2 seconds to enter calibration — the Home light flashes slowly in white. With nothing touching the sticks or triggers, press A once. Then rotate both sticks in full circles 2-3 times and fully press both triggers three times, and press A to exit.

faq.q: How do I switch between XInput, Switch, and Android/other input modes?
faq.a: Hold the [-] (View) and [+] (Menu) buttons to cycle through XInput, Switch and other-device modes. This only works in dongle and wired modes, not over Bluetooth. In XInput mode, indicator lights 2 and 4 illuminate.

faq.q: How do I reset the controller?
faq.a: There are two resets. For a hardware force-off when the controller will not power on or off, press the recessed Reset button in the circular hole on the back with a paperclip. To reset the profile and all settings, hold Home + Menu until the Logo button blinks (GameSir's support FAQ specifies 5 seconds, until the Logo LED flashes green twice).

faq.q: How long does the battery last, and how do I check the level?
faq.a: GameSir's estimate, provided to TechRadar on request, is about 15 hours from the 1000mAh cell; no figure is published on the product page. There is no percentage readout in the software or on the controller — the only battery indicator is the Home light flashing red when charge drops below 15%. The controller auto-powers-off after 10 minutes of inactivity.

faq.q: Does it work with Xbox consoles?
faq.a: No. The Super Nova supports PC, Switch, Android and iOS only. Xbox consoles require an Xbox-licensed GameSir model.

faq.q: Can I change the button layout?
faq.a: Yes, in two ways. Physically, both the middle faceplate and the ABXY buttons are detachable so you can rearrange the caps. In firmware, hold M + the south face button to swap the A-B and X-Y button values.

controllers.name: GameSir Tarantula Pro
controllers.tagline: A tri-mode multiplatform controller with a symmetric PlayStation-style stick layout, Mag-Res TMR sticks, and a motorized gear that physically rotates the face buttons between Xbox and Nintendo layouts.
controllers.msrp: $79.99 / £79.99 at launch (October 2024); currently listed at $69.99 on gamesir.com

connectivity.notes: Tri-mode: USB-C wired, 2.4GHz dongle, Bluetooth. Variant differences: the 'Tarantula Pro for Xbox' is WIRED-ONLY (3m detachable USB-C, no battery, 4 rumble motors, micro-switch ABXY, 3.5mm jack, 235g) and uses GameSir Nexus rather than Connect; the 'Tarantula 8K PC' is also wired-only (1.8m cable, PC only, 8000Hz, Gen-2 TMR, no rumble, no battery, 180g). The 'With Dock' / Bundle Edition is the same controller shipped with a charging station.

sticks.tech: GameSir Mag-Res TMR (Gen-1) — tunneling magnetoresistance, non-contact
sticks.measuredNotes: Measured by gamepadla Stick Tracer on firmware 2.0.6, single unit. Note gamepadla lists this controller under its former name, T3 Pro.

triggers.tech: Hall Effect analog triggers with a physical gear that converts them to micro-switch triggers
triggers.notes: Three states are documented by GameSir: Hall Effect analog mode (linear, for racing), Hall Effect hair-trigger mode (enabled via a key combo — GameSir does not state which combo on the pages reviewed), and micro-switch mode selected by moving the physical trigger gear.

controllers.dpad: Four-way tactile-switch D-pad, positioned upper-left in a symmetric DualShock-style arrangement. Not swappable or replaceable.
controllers.faceButtons: Four membrane ABXY buttons with no printed symbols. A motorized internal gear physically rotates the cluster between Xbox and Nintendo layouts, visible through a transparent window; the buttons are LED-lit and change color with the selected layout. Reviewers report the combo is M + A (Xbox) or M + B (Switch) held ~2 seconds; GameSir's FAQ states 'hold for 2 seconds until the gear rotates' but shows the combo only as an image. Membrane switches are the most commonly criticized part of the controller.

pollingRate.pc: 1000 Hz (wired and 2.4GHz dongle); Gamepadla measured 1000-1002 Hz median wired and 1000-1001 Hz via dongle
pollingRate.notes: Not an Xbox-compatible model — the separate 'Tarantula Pro for Xbox' is rated 1000Hz on PC and 250Hz on Xbox console. Bluetooth is much slower: Gamepadla measured a 162 Hz median polling rate in Sony/DS4 mode. Gamepadla LatScore is B wired / D wireless, with measured wired button latency of 7.83 ms and dongle button latency of 31.7 ms on firmware 2.0.6 — notably worse than the Cyclone 2.

battery.claimedLife: No battery-life figure is published on the gamesir.com product page, FAQ, or manual. GameSir's regional official store (gamesir.sa) claims 'up to 25 hours playtime, depending on RGB lighting usage and connection method.'
battery.notes: GameRant states GameSir provides no specific battery-life figure, and measured approximately 20 hours over Bluetooth with RGB at maximum brightness. Treat 25 hours as an unconfirmed regional-store claim, not a headline manufacturer spec.

controllers.weight: 263 g / 0.58 lbs (Standard Edition, controller only). GameSir lists 325 g / 0.72 lbs net weight for the Bundle Edition, which includes the charging station.

extraButtons.notes: Nine remappable buttons in total: R4, L4 (back buttons), C1, C2, C3, C4, T1, T2, T3. Each can be mapped to a single button or a sequence of up to 12. GameSir's documentation for the Tarantula Pro does not classify T1/T2 — on the Tarantula 8K PC the same T1/T2 names are described as 'extra bumpers,' but a GamesRadar hands-on describes the Tarantula Pro's extra front controls as four small buttons around the center panel plus an actuator on either side of it, so extraBumpers is left null rather than guessed. Physical back-button latches on the rear mechanically disable L4/R4 to prevent accidental input.

gyro.notes: Built-in 6-axis gyroscope, supports motion control on Switch. The controller also has NFC for amiibo interaction with Nintendo devices and can wake the Switch with a single press.

controllers.rumble: HD Rumble with 2 motors, per GameSir's official FAQ. Note the 'Tarantula Pro for Xbox' variant instead has 4 motors (one in each grip and each trigger), and the Tarantula 8K PC has none.

faceplates.notes: No magnetic or swappable faceplate system is documented for this model. Visual customization comes from the rotating face-button gear, the RGB light strip, the RGB Home indicator, and the illuminated face buttons.

controllers.software: GameSir Connect (PC) and the GameSir app (mobile). GameSir Nexus does not support this model. Worth knowing: GameSir's downloads page does not list the multiplatform Tarantula Pro under any application — it lists only the Tarantula 8K PC under Connect and Tarantula Pro for Xbox under Nexus — while the official Tarantula Pro FAQ directs users to Connect. Treat the FAQ as authoritative and the downloads listing as incomplete.
notableFeatures: Motorized gear physically rotates the unlabeled ABXY cluster between Xbox and Nintendo layouts, with a transparent window showing the mechanism
Symmetric PlayStation-style stick layout, unusual for a Switch/PC controller
Nine remappable buttons, each supporting sequences of up to 12 inputs
Five extra buttons on the front face arranged in three rows (C1-C4 and T3) — GameSir's stated 'tarantula' design inspiration
Physical back-button latches mechanically disable L4/R4
Triggers switch between Hall Effect analog, Hall Effect hair-trigger, and micro-switch via a physical gear
NFC support for amiibo plus one-press Switch wake
Turbo with four modes: Slow 8Hz, Medium 12Hz, Fast 20Hz, Off
On-controller RGB editing by holding M plus a stick or the D-pad (effect, animation speed, brightness, color, saturation)

knownIssues.symptom: Double-clicking D-pad, reversed/reverted joystick axes, low polling rate, and the controller not being recognized by GameSir Connect over the dongle.
knownIssues.cause: GameSir states there were many bugs in early firmware versions of the Tarantula Pro, in both the controller and the dongle.
knownIssues.fix: Update BOTH the controller and dongle firmware to the latest version. Controller: connect via USB, open the updater, press Logo + X + Y simultaneously until the device status shows online, then click update firmware. Dongle: exit GameSir Connect, insert the receiver, hold the pairing button for 5 seconds until Device Status shows ONLINE in green, then click Upgrade Firmware. WARNING: GameSir provides different controller firmware files by serial number (V2.06 for SN starting with 1 or 2, a separate V2.06 for SN starting with 3) and warns that the wrong file may brick the controller.

knownIssues.symptom: GameSir Nexus does not detect the Tarantula Pro at all.
knownIssues.cause: Wrong application. The multiplatform Tarantula Pro is a GameSir Connect device; Nexus is only for GameSir's Xbox-licensed controllers (including the separate 'Tarantula Pro for Xbox').
knownIssues.fix: Use GameSir Connect, connected via dongle or cable in XInput mode. GameSir explicitly notes Connect will not detect the controller when it is in DS or NS mode over a Bluetooth connection.

knownIssues.symptom: Apparent stick drift straight out of the box after setting the initial deadzone to 0 in GameSir Connect.
knownIssues.cause: Not a defect. A 0 deadzone is a true physical zero, which makes the stick extremely sensitive to any resting-position noise.
knownIssues.fix: Set the inner deadzone to 3-5 in GameSir Connect.

knownIssues.symptom: Cannot connect over Bluetooth or dongle; the indicator light keeps blinking slowly.
knownIssues.cause: Slow blinking means the controller is in reconnecting mode, trying to reach a previously paired device, rather than in pairing mode.
knownIssues.fix: Hold the Pairing Button on the controller for 2 seconds to force pairing mode — the light should then blink fast. For a dongle connection, also hold the pairing button on the dongle until it blinks fast so the two re-pair.

knownIssues.symptom: Stick drift or trigger inaccuracy during use.
knownIssues.cause: Sticks and/or triggers have lost calibration.
knownIssues.fix: Run the on-board Stick & Trigger Calibration procedure documented in the manual; GameSir links a video calibration tutorial from the FAQ page.

knownIssues.symptom: Higher-than-expected input latency, especially over the 2.4GHz dongle.
knownIssues.cause: Firmware/internal processing rather than polling rate. The controller reports a genuine 1000 Hz polling rate, but measured hardware latency is much higher than similarly specced GameSir models.
knownIssues.fix: No documented fix. Gamepadla measured 7.83 ms average button latency wired and 31.73 ms via dongle on firmware 2.0.6, versus 2.33 ms wired for the Cyclone 2, and rates it B wired / D wireless. Prefer the wired connection for latency-sensitive play and keep firmware current.

faq.q: Which software do I need — GameSir Nexus or GameSir Connect?
faq.a: GameSir Connect, connected via dongle or cable in XInput mode. GameSir Nexus does not recognize the multiplatform Tarantula Pro. Connect also will not see the controller if it is in DS or NS mode over Bluetooth. The mobile GameSir app can also configure it. (The separate 'Tarantula Pro for Xbox' is the opposite case — it uses GameSir Nexus.)

faq.q: What platforms does the Tarantula Pro support?
faq.a: PC, Switch, iOS, Android, and Steam. It does not support Xbox consoles — that requires the separate wired 'Tarantula Pro for Xbox' model.

faq.q: How do I change the face button layout between Xbox and Nintendo?
faq.a: GameSir's FAQ says to hold the combo for 2 seconds until the gear rotates and changes both the layout and the key values; the default is the Xbox layout. Reviewers document the combo as M + A for the Xbox layout and M + B for the Switch layout. The buttons physically rotate and change color to match.

faq.q: How many remappable buttons are there and what can they do?
faq.a: Nine: R4, L4, C1, C2, C3, C4, T1, T2, T3. Each can be mapped to a single button or a sequence of up to 12. Assignable values include A, B, X, Y, LB, RB, LT, RT, LS, RS, View, Menu, D-pad, and both sticks.

faq.q: What do the back button latches do?
faq.a: They mechanically enable or disable the L4/R4 back buttons so you can prevent unintended input when you are not using them.

faq.q: How do I pair the Tarantula Pro to a phone over Bluetooth?
faq.a: Hold the controller's combo for 2 seconds until channel indicators 1 and 5 flash, then release. Open your phone's Bluetooth list, find 'GameSir- Tarantula Pro' and connect. The channel indicator goes solid when connected.

faq.q: Does it have a turbo/rapid-fire function?
faq.a: Yes, with four modes: Slow (8Hz), Medium (12Hz), Fast (20Hz), and Off.

faq.q: How many rumble motors does it have?
faq.a: Two HD rumble motors. This differs by variant: the wired 'Tarantula Pro for Xbox' has four (one in each grip and each trigger), and the Tarantula 8K PC has none.
